calls.video_title: PROOF These 5 Stocks Will Make Millionaires
calls.thesis: Favorite cybersecurity name for balance of growth and profitability: revenue +20%, operating profitability 33% (best among pure-play cyber), $2.8B free cash flow, product revenue +37% last quarter. Holds 500 shares at $88 cost, +48% so far.
calls.base_case: Gartner expects AI-driven cybersecurity spending +68% to $86B in 2027; enterprise cyber budgets cannot be cut (average hack costs $5M+).
calls.bull_case: Multiple re-rates to 45x P/E on $3.56 EPS -> $160 fair value as the market reprices cybersecurity on higher demand.
calls.bear_case: All cyber names trade steep P/E and P/S; software stocks shunned on fears AI/vibe coding replaces software services.

calls.thesis: 35% EBITDA margin, the best profitability in the cybersecurity group; integrated security and networking hardware with custom ASIC technology; 2.2x PEG is relatively good value; last quarter's disappointment front-loaded revenue and he expects a bounce-back in the shares.
Revenue +20%, product revenue +37%, billings +29% is good, but growth is decelerating (Q4 guide +17.8%, analysts expect sub-10% by end-2027) and 27x FCF is still too high for a slowing business.
calls.price_at_call: 27x free cash flow (was ~40x before earnings); no share price stated; down 35% from recent highs

calls.thesis: 'I'd be picking up more shares of Fortinet' after a 37% monthly drop on a marginal $40M service-revenue guidance trim, despite 22% revenue growth and $865M FCF.

Start accumulating after a 24% weekly fall on an otherwise impressive Q3 (revenue +20%, $0.91 EPS, $865M free cash flow, full-year guidance raised): product growth slowed to 37% from 52% and Q4 guides 20%, but AI-driven security demand and a 38% operating margin support the longer-term story. Still not cheap at 37x expected $3.57 EPS, but last year's 32x low implies ~$114.
calls.price_at_call: ~$114 at last year's 32x low; 37x expected $3.57 EPS now

calls.thesis: Conditional buy / buy on dips, softening the earnings-week stance: he holds 500 Fortinet shares as one of five cybersecurity names ($300k+ across the group) and reports Wednesday, with ~20% revenue growth and 25% earnings growth to $3.45 expected, but after a 118% rise this year the valuation is 61x earnings (nearly double December's 32x) and ~3.1x on a PEG basis, so upside around earnings looks limited and he would not load up now; he would buy any big dip.
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; up 118% this year; 61x earnings, ~3.1x PEG; analyst average target roughly at the current price

calls.thesis: Explicit pause: he probably would not pick up a whole lot more Fortinet (or Okta) just yet — at ~3x price-to-earnings adjusted for growth it is a little more expensive versus its history, in slower-growing segments (15% growth), though profitability is its strength. Down from his prior BUY stance.
calls.price_at_call: No price stated; down ~7% on Friday and ~13% over five days

calls.thesis: Second-cheapest cyber at 3.1x PEG; 15% revenue growth — 'I would be picking up shares of Fortinet and Zscaler' on the broader cybersecurity theme.
